title: Valuation and P/E
summary: P/E = price ÷ EPS. Earnings yield = EPS ÷ price. Dividend yield and payout ratio show how much profit comes back as cash. A good business can be a poor investment at a high price.
unreliableWhen: When earnings are zero or negative, when one year's profit is unusual, or when a low P/E reflects a business that is shrinking.
goodExample: A fictional food maker on a P/E near 12 with steady profit: the price assumes little growth, so modest results do not need to surprise anyone.
badExample: A fictional app maker on a P/E of 80: even fast growth may leave the price looking high, and if growth slows the price has a long way to fall.
